facts: $|x|$ is the distance of $x$ from $0$ on a number line, so $|x| \ge 0$ for all real numbers.
Opposite numbers have equal absolute value: $|-x| = |x|$ for all real numbers $x$.
The distance between two numbers $a$ and $b$ on a number line is $|a - b| = |b - a|$.
Power property: $|a|^2 = a^2$ for all real numbers $a$.
For real numbers $a$ and $b$, $|a+b|\le |a|+|b|$. You can check this for given values by evaluating the two sides.
Work out what is inside the absolute value signs first, then find its distance from zero. Apply operations outside the signs afterwards.

workedExamples.question_text: Find the distance between $-9$ and $4$ on a number line, using an absolute value expression.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$|4-(-9)|=|13|$
$|13|=13$
The distance is $13$ units.
The other order gives $|-9-4|=|-13|=13$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Using $|ab|=|a||b|$, evaluate $|-6\times7|$.
(b) Check that $|a+b|\le|a|+|b|$ for $a=-9$ and $b=4$ by calculating both sides.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $|-6\times7|=|-6|\times|7|$
$|-6|\times|7|=6\times7$
$6\times7=42$
(b) $\text{LHS}=|-9+4|=|-5|=5$
$\text{RHS}=|-9|+|4|=9+4=13$
Since $5\le13$, the inequality holds for these values. The two sides are not equal.

development.question_text:
The distance between two numbers $x$ and $-3$ on a number line is given by $|x - (-3)|$.
Find this distance when $x = -11$.
Check that $|a+b|\le |a|+|b|$ for $a=-6$ and $b=4$ by calculating both sides.
development.solution_text:
$\text{LHS}=|-6+4|=|-2|=2$
$\text{RHS}=|-6|+|4|=6+4=10$
Since $2\le10$, the inequality holds for these values.

mastery.question_text:
Use the piecewise definition to write $|x|$ without absolute value signs for:
(a) $x<0$
(b) $x=0$
(c) $x>0$.

The coordinates of points $P, Q, R$ on a number line are $-7, 1, 9$ respectively.
Determine whether the distance between $P$ and $R$ equals the sum of the distances from $P$ to $Q$ and $Q$ to $R$.
mastery.solution_text:
$PQ=|1-(-7)|=|8|=8$
$QR=|9-1|=|8|=8$
$PR=|9-(-7)|=|16|=16$
$PQ+QR=8+8=16=PR$
Yes. Both routes have a distance of $16$ units.
